description: NBT Central, crediting Chanthaburi provincial public relations, reported that the Royal Thai Armed Forces led nine ASEAN Observer Team-Thailand delegates from Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines to Chanthaburi on July 1. The delegation received briefings on border management, security, transnational-crime prevention and the border security fence project, then inspected locations including the fence alignment between boundary markers 52 and 59. The report says the mission began in the morning but does not give an exact event time.

description: Cambodia's Foreign Ministry said Thai armed forces installed barbed wire on July 2 at Mom Bei in Preah Vihear province and Chob Ruan in Trapeang Prasat district, Oddar Meanchey. Cambodia alleged that the work violated the December 27, 2025 GBC Joint Statement and Article 5 of the 2000 land-boundary MOU. The installation and legal characterization remain Cambodia's account in the cited evidence.

description: AEC TV Online reported that on the morning of July 2, Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters led AOT-TH to Trat province. The delegation began at the Ban Hat Lek permanent border crossing in Khlong Yai district, inspected the area around boundary marker 73 and a nearby sediment-control structure built by a Cambodian private entity, and later received briefings on recovered landmines. The report gives no exact event time. Its coastal-impact characterization reflects information provided by Thai officials in the cited report.

description: On July 4, Cambodia's Foreign Ministry issued a formal protest over what it said were Thai barbed-wire installations carried out on July 2 at Mom Bei and Chob Ruan. Cambodia said the alleged work breached the December 27, 2025 GBC Joint Statement and Article 5 of the 2000 land-boundary MOU and called for the activities to stop. The protest establishes Cambodia's diplomatic action and position, not independent proof of the underlying territorial claim.
descriptionKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 4 ខែកក្កដា ក្រសួងការបរទេសកម្ពុជាបានចេញលិខិតតវ៉ាជាផ្លូវការចំពោះអ្វីដែលកម្ពុជានិយាយថា ជាការដំឡើងលួសបន្លារបស់ថៃកាលពីថ្ងៃទី 2 ខែកក្កដា នៅមុំបី និងចបរួន។ កម្ពុជាបាននិយាយថាសកម្មភាពដែលត្រូវបានចោទប្រកាន់នេះរំលោភសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍រួម GBC ថ្ងៃទី 27 ខែធ្នូ ឆ្នាំ 2025 និងមាត្រា 5 នៃ MOU ឆ្នាំ 2000 ស្តីពីព្រំដែនគោក ហើយបានអំពាវនាវឱ្យបញ្ឈប់សកម្មភាពទាំងនោះ។ ការតវ៉ានេះបញ្ជាក់ពីសកម្មភាពការទូត និងជំហររបស់កម្ពុជា មិនមែនជាភស្តុតាងឯករាជ្យអំពីការអះអាងដែនដីមូលដ្ឋានទេ។
descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 4 กรกฎาคม กระทรวงการต่างประเทศกัมพูชาออกหนังสือประท้วงอย่างเป็นทางการต่อสิ่งที่กัมพูชาระบุว่าเป็นการติดตั้งลวดหนามของไทยเมื่อวันที่ 2 กรกฎาคมที่มุมเบยและช็อบรวน กัมพูชาระบุว่าการดำเนินการดังกล่าวละเมิดแถลงการณ์ร่วม GBC วันที่ 27 ธันวาคม 2025 และมาตรา 5 ของ MOU ปี 2000 ว่าด้วยเขตแดนทางบก และเรียกร้องให้ยุติกิจกรรมดังกล่าว การประท้วงนี้ยืนยันว่ากัมพูชาได้ดำเนินการทางการทูตและแสดงจุดยืน แต่ไม่ได้เป็นหลักฐานอิสระยืนยันข้อพิพาทเรื่องอธิปไตย

description: On July 3, Cambodia's Acting Foreign Minister Eat Sophea briefed 42 representatives of diplomatic missions and international organisations in Phnom Penh on Cambodia's account of the border situation. She said early resumption of Joint Boundary Commission survey and demarcation work was important for de-escalation, trust-building and the return of displaced residents, and reiterated Cambodia's stated commitment to peaceful settlement. description: Cambodia's Defence Ministry said that at approximately 12:35 on July 5, a Cambodian patrol in Banteay Ampil district, Oddar Meanchey, passed a Thai patrol on the opposite side of a barbed-wire fence before an explosive device detonated behind the Cambodian patrol, wounding four soldiers with shrapnel. Cambodia said the cause was under investigation and did not assign responsibility in its official statement. Thailand denied that its forces caused the blast and later said its inquiry pointed to an explosion on Cambodian-controlled territory, while advancing a landmine explanation. description: On July 6, the ASEAN Observer Team assigned to Cambodia, led by the Philippine Head of Mission, inspected the border between Boundary Markers 52 and 59 in Kamrieng district, Battambang province. Near Markers 52 to 54, Cambodia’s Defence Ministry said the team inspected a fence it alleges was unilaterally constructed by the Thai military and witnessed damage to temporary markers. Cambodia urged the Joint Boundary Commission to agree the boundary alignment before permanent construction proceeds. Thai authorities separately told ASEAN observers that the fence project was within Thai territory, complied with international law, and was intended to improve border security. The cited report presents the two sides’ positions and does not independently determine sovereignty or responsibility for the marker damage.

description: On July 17, Chinese President Xi Jinping held separate meetings in Shanghai with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet. In China's Foreign Ministry account of the meeting with Anutin, Xi said peaceful handling of the Thailand-Cambodia border dispute served both countries' long-term interests, urged dialogue and consultation, and said China was ready to continue playing a constructive role. In the separate meeting with Hun Manet, Xi said consolidating the ceasefire and gradually rebuilding mutual trust served Cambodia and Thailand's long-term interests, supported a solution through dialogue and negotiation, and said China was ready to continue playing a positive role. The two official Chinese readouts also said Anutin and Hun Manet each affirmed commitment to peaceful resolution or de-escalation.

description: At its 14:00 briefing on July 17, Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Thailand and Cambodia had agreed to extend the deadline for the four appointed UNCLOS conciliators to select a fifth conciliator and chair from July 19 to August 14, following a proposal from the conciliators for more time to identify a suitable and mutually acceptable candidate. description: On July 22, Cambodia's Foreign Ministry formally protested activities it said Thai armed forces had carried out in Oddar Meanchey province: road construction between Boundary Pillars 8 and 9 in Ta Tum from July 13–15, followed by further road work and barbed-wire installation between Pillars 19 and 20 in Chup Doeum Khnol from July 15–19. Cambodia alleged the works extended into Cambodian territory and violated its sovereignty, Article 5 of the 2000 land-border MOU and the December 27, 2025 GBC Joint Statement, and urged Thailand to stop the activities. These territorial and legal claims are Cambodia's position; the cited statement does not include Thailand's response.

description: At 13:00 on July 22, Thai Chief of Defence Forces Gen Ukrit Boontanon inspected the Chanthaburi border-fence project in Pong Nam Ron district. A Thai military briefing said the 1.31-kilometre section between boundary markers 52 and 54 was 78.56% complete: 350 metres were complete except for finishing work, 450 metres were receiving concertina wire, and 410 metres remained under construction on sloped terrain. Officials said high-strength concrete components had passed small-arms-fire tests. Reuters reported the same day that Thailand had completed the first section, but the detailed Thai briefing showed construction was still ongoing.

description: On July 23 in Manila, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn to discuss U.S.-Cambodia cooperation bilaterally and through ASEAN. According to the U.S. Department of State readout, they reaffirmed a shared commitment to implementing the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords and to deeper law-enforcement cooperation, including on scam centers. The readout does not provide an exact meeting time.

description: On July 24, authorities repatriated 36 Thai nationals from Cambodia and returned 67 Cambodian nationals through the Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Sa Kaeo. Bangkok Post reporting republished by Inkl said the exchange was carried out under bilateral legal and humanitarian cooperation by the Burapha Task Force, immigration, customs, border patrol and other agencies. The 67 Cambodians comprised 43 men, 21 women and three boys, all of whom had completed legal proceedings and served their sentences in Thailand before being returned.

descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 24 กรกฎาคม ทางการรับคนไทย 36 คนกลับจากกัมพูชา และส่งชาวกัมพูชา 67 คนกลับประเทศผ่านจุดผ่านแดนคลองลึก จังหวัดสระแก้ว รายงานของ Bangkok Post ที่เผยแพร่ซ้ำโดย Inkl ระบุว่า การส่งมอบดำเนินการภายใต้ความร่วมมือด้านกฎหมายและมนุษยธรรม โดยมีกองกำลังบูรพา ตำรวจตรวจคนเข้าเมือง ศุลกากร ตำรวจตระเวนชายแดน และหน่วยงานอื่นร่วมดำเนินการ ชาวกัมพูชา 67 คนประกอบด้วยชาย 43 คน หญิง 21 คน และเด็กชาย 3 คน ซึ่งทั้งหมดผ่านกระบวนการทางกฎหมายและรับโทษในไทยครบแล้วก่อนถูกส่งกลับ

description: On July 24, Chinese Defence Minister Admiral Dong Jun met Thai Defence Minister Lt. Gen. Adul Boonthamcharoen in Bangkok. After the talks, Adul said Dong had reaffirmed China's neutral position in the Thailand–Cambodia dispute because both countries are friends of China. Adul also said Chinese military equipment supplied to Cambodia was tied to existing agreements and that deliveries would be delayed during active fighting. These neutrality and supply-policy points are attributed to Adul's account of the meeting; the cited reports do not independently establish China's internal policy decisions.

description: On July 27, UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Cambodia Tom Andrews visited the Boeung Trakuon area in Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey, with provincial governor Oum Reatrey and local officials to observe security and humanitarian conditions. Cambodian officials showed him an area where they said Thai military personnel had placed shipping containers and razor wire. The visit formed part of his mission examining human-rights impacts of the border conflict.

description: On July 29 at the Ban Khlong Luek international crossing in Sa Kaeo, Col. Bancha Chanchalad, deputy chief of the Thai-Cambodian Border Coordination Office, met Brig. Gen. Lai Khem Huot, deputy chief of the Cambodian-Thai Border Coordination Office. The two sides agreed to strengthen humanitarian coordination, said crossings would remain closed except for citizen repatriation, asked border forces to follow the December 27, 2025 ceasefire and the 2000 land-boundary MOU, and agreed to avoid provocative actions and keep communication channels open.

descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 29 กรกฎาคม ที่จุดผ่านแดนถาวรบ้านคลองลึก จังหวัดสระแก้ว พ.อ.บัญชา ชาญฉลาด รองหัวหน้าสำนักงานประสานงานชายแดนไทย–กัมพูชา พบกับ พลจัตวา Lai Khem Huot รองหัวหน้าสำนักงานประสานงานชายแดนกัมพูชา–ไทย ทั้งสองฝ่ายตกลงเสริมการประสานงานด้านมนุษยธรรม ระบุว่าด่านชายแดนจะยังปิดอยู่ยกเว้นการส่งกลับพลเมือง ขอให้กำลังในพื้นที่ปฏิบัติตามข้อตกลงหยุดยิงวันที่ 27 ธันวาคม 2025 และ MOU เขตแดนทางบกปี 2000 พร้อมหลีกเลี่ยงการกระทำยั่วยุและคงช่องทางการสื่อสารไว้

description: At about 11:00 on July 29, a technical survey officer working with Humanitarian Mine Action Unit 1 stepped on a PMN anti-personnel mine in a confirmed hazardous area at Ban Nong Chan, Sa Kaeo. The Nation/ANN report carried by The Star said the officer lost his left leg and suffered severe injuries to his right leg and left arm. The team suspended the operation, gave emergency aid and evacuated him to Aranyaprathet Hospital. The report identifies the mine type and injury from Thai operational reporting; it does not independently establish when or by whom the mine was laid.
